subject: Meridian tranche: urgent allocation guidance and shortfall mitigation
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@meridiansys.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@meridiansys.com
Date: 2028-07-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected peak — need to increase dedicated tranche for Q3

Hi Mateo,

Quick context: we ramped a new inference-heavy feature last week and are seeing steady 3x above forecasted token QPS during business hours. Our analytics team flagged sustained latency bumps for our customer-facing flows and asked us to reach out.

We have an active Dedicated tranche with Redwood (Committed: 4x A100-equivalent slots). Based on early telemetry, we expect to need 50% more baseline capacity to meet SLA for the next 60 days.

Ask: can we get a temporary tranche increase (either preemptible or reserved) to bridge the next two months while we finish model optimization? We can sign a short addendum for the uplift if needed.

Procurement is looped on cc for approvals. We are sensitive to both cost and risk of preemption — any guidance on prioritization against other reserved customers is appreciated.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Platform Engineering
Meridian Systems

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@meridiansys.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected peak — need to increase dedicated tranche for Q3

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the details, this is the right time to escalate. A few quick clarifying Qs before I pull ops into a schedule: 

- Current sustained token QPS (business hours) and projected peak QPS (if available).
- Tolerance for preemption vs guaranteed throughput (you mentioned sensitivity to preemption).
- Is Meridian open to a hybrid approach: modest reserved uplift + short-lived burst credits to avoid immediate long-term commits?

I'll run this through capacity and sales tradeoffs with Ben and Laura. If you can attach a short telemetry export (hourly QPS last 7 days) that helps triage quickly.


--
Mateo Alvarez
Account Lead, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-29T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected peak — need to increase dedicated tranche for Q3

Team — summarizing our constraints and a proposal: 

Constraint summary:
- Available pool: we have two A100-equivalent tranches free in region-us-west for the next 45 days before scheduled commitments (see INF-9123).
- Reserved capacity claims: three mid-tier reserved customers (Tiers B/C) are already queued for planned scaling on Aug 15; preemption risk increases after that window.

Proposal for Meridian (fastest path to reduce risk):
1) Immediate uplift: provide +2 A100-equivalent reserved slots for 30 days, auto-convert to burst credits (preemptible) beyond day 30 unless Meridian signs an addendum to extend. Cost uplift: ~+28% monthly over current commit.
2) Fallback: if Meridian declines reserved uplift, offer 100k burst-credit tokens (non-guaranteed) for 30 days with preemption under high load.

Operational asks: we need telemetry export (hourly QPS) and a signed MAP (mutual action plan) by EOD Jul 30 to lock the reserved uplift before the Aug 15 queue reshuffle. I attached a draft MAP and tranche worksheet for quick sign-off.

Atts: meridian-proposed-tranche-v2.pdf (proposal), Mural-MAP-meridian.xlsx (mutual action plan template)

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-29T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected peak — need to increase dedicated tranche for Q3

Ben — thanks for the proposal. A few prioritization rules from Capacity Ops to call out (so Sales and Account understand escalation behavior):

1) Short-term reserved uplift (<=30 days) can be granted from uncommitted pool if: 1) customer has active commit (yes), 2) signed MAP in 48h, and 3) their usage profile indicates stable uplift (not a 48h spike).
2) Beyond 30 days we require either an amendment (signed PO/commit) or conversion to burst credits.
3) In queue conflicts (Aug 15 reshuffle) we prioritize by: committed annual $ > platform-critical workloads > first-come signed addendum.

Given Meridian's ARR and their live production SLA, approve the +2 reserved slots for 30 days contingent on telemetry and a signed MAP by COB Jul 30. Rishi, please reserve tranche identifiers and tag as "temp-reserve-meridian-5872" in the allocator.

Laura Bennett
Head, Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@meridiansys.com>, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, procurement@meridiansys.com
Date: 2028-07-30T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected peak — need to increase dedicated tranche for Q3 (Allocation confirmed)

Elena — following Laura's guidance and the MAP Ben provided, we have provisioned a temporary tranche: 

- Allocation: +2 A100-equivalent reserved slots (tag: temp-reserve-meridian-5872)
- Effective: 2028-07-30 17:00 PDT
- Term: 30 days; will convert to preemptible burst on 2028-08-29 17:00 PDT unless an amendment signed earlier.
- Cost: +28% monthly on top of current commit (pricing sheet in MAP).

Attached: tranche assignment record (internal) and MAP draft (Meridian copy).

Notes: we flagged the tranche in INF-9123 so scheduling won't allocate those slots to queued deals on Aug 15. If Meridian can provide the telemetry export and a countersigned MAP by EOD Jul 31 we will extend consideration for a longer reserved amendment.

Rishi Malhotra
Capacity Planner | Redwood Inference

Attachments: meridian-proposed-tranche-v2.pdf, Mural-MAP-meridian.xlsx
